name: R Draconis
type: Mira variable: a pulsating red giant star
summary: R Draconis is an aging giant star, far bigger than the Sun, that swells and shrinks. As it pulsates, its visible brightness rises and falls every 246 days, about eight months.
why_interesting: It shows the other way a star can change brightness: not dust passing in front, but the whole star pulsating. In infrared light it is so bright that it saturates the SPHEREx detectors, so SkyShift shows its images but not a brightness curve.

facts.label: Distance
facts.compare: Gaia DR3 parallax 1.2509 ± 0.0648 mas (799 ± 41 parsecs). Parallaxes of large pulsating giants are less reliable, because the star's bright centre shifts as it pulsates. Not used: Gaia DR2, which gave about 2,160 light-years; DR3 is newer and more precise.

facts.label: Pulsation period
facts.compare: About eight months from one brightness peak to the next.

facts.label: Brightness range (visible, V)
facts.compare: At its brightest it is about 400 times brighter than at its faintest.

facts.label: Infrared brightness (2MASS J)
facts.compare: About 75 to 100 times brighter than RW Aurigae or UX Orionis at this wavelength: that is why it saturates SPHEREx.
